name: Corpay, Inc. (formerly FLEETCOR)

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Corpay calls itself the Global Spend Management Company: it sells fuel cards, B2B payables and cross-border payments, and lodging payments to businesses.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $1,382M: Vehicle Payments 42%, Corporate Payments 41% (35% a year ago), Lodging 9%, Other 7%. Corporate Payments revenue +41% reported (+18% organic); Vehicle +8%; Lodging +3%.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Businesses of all sizes (fleets, corporates, hotels/travel). No single-customer concentration found in the Q3 release or 10-Q text read; late fees and finance charges ~3% of 9M revenue, float ~3%.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: 9M 2026 revenue: US 44% (50% a year ago), Brazil 16%, UK 15%, Other 24%. More than half is foreign, so a strong dollar cuts translated revenue (dollar +4.8% in 3m).

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Fees and interchange as a percent of spend (fuel cards, payables, FX margin) plus small float and late-fee income; recurring in nature because customers re-buy fuel/payments, but not subscription. Corporate Payments EBITDA margin 57.4% in Q3.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: High operating leverage: Q3 adjusted EBITDA $793.8M (+17%) on revenue +18%. 9M capex $143M vs operating cash flow $716M (capex about 3.6% of revenue). Management hit/raised guidance: Q3 revenue and EPS 'ahead of expectations', FY26 outlook raised to $5.35B revenue, $28.00 adj EPS at midpoint.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical inputs: retail fuel merchants/networks (diffuse, tag: oil, inflation), bank funding (revolver $2.76B drawn, securitization $2.3B; tag: rates, hy_spreads), FX dealers/partners for cross-border (tag: dollar). Fuel revenue is partly percent of price: guide assumes $4.90/gal for rest of 2026 and flat fuel spreads, so oil -18% in a month is a headwind to Vehicle (42% of revenue). Interest expense guide $435-455M cannot be passed on to customers; fuel price and FX effects are only partly passed through. No single point of failure named in what was read.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Scale and acquiring-side network in fuel cards, cross-border FX with hedging expertise, distribution of corporate payments (AvidXchange stake, Alpha acquired Oct 2025). Doing differently now: rotating to corporate payments and a $1.1B minority stake in BILL with option to buy 100% (in 2030).

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: B2B brand; end users (drivers, hotel bookers) do not choose it. Not an everyday consumer brand; customers would notice but could switch cards. No marketing-per-revenue figure read.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Rivals in fuel cards and payables include WEX, Fleet-related bank cards and AvidXchange/BILL-type platforms. Organic growth 11% in five of last six quarters points to share gains or market growth; no independent share data read.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Corporate Payments organic +18% in Q3 and now 41% of revenue; BILL (SMB payables, accountant distribution) widens the runway. Vehicle +8% reported and sensitive to fuel price.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: 2025 operating cash flow $1,500M less capex $201M = $1.30B FCF (vs $1.39B in 2020; flat, noisy). Total debt $11.23B vs unrestricted cash $3.07B at 9/30/26; $1.85B buybacks YTD (5.25M shares). Pay: ~90% of NEO pay in stock, incentive tied to published guidance (DEF 14A). Insider ownership % not extracted.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Payments for fleets, hotels and corporate payables are ongoing needs; Corporate Payments is gaining relevance. Risk: EV adoption shrinks fuel-card base over time; key-person risk on CEO Ron Clarke (also chairman).

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 8-K Item 4.01/4.02 or NT filing in the 40 most recent filings (Jun 2024 to Nov 2026). FTC case: Eleventh Circuit affirmed liability Jan 2026; proposed consent order agreed Jul 1 2026, $100M charge booked, still needs FTC Commissioners and court approval. Non-GAAP gap: Q3 adj EPS $7.54 vs GAAP $5.66.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: fuel price tailwind and float income (+) but dollar up (-). Slowdown: freight, travel and spend volumes soften, credit losses rise; cross-border and Corporate Payments steadier. Stagflation: fuel pass-through helps, volumes and credit hurt. Boom: positive.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: FTC consent order pending approval (extra redress possible if changed); CFPB/AML and foreign regulators across Brazil/UK named in risk text; BILL deal needs shareholder and regulatory approval, expected close first half 2027.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $454.33 (11/25 close, 52w range $281-$480), market cap $29.1B, EV ~$37.2B using $11.2B debt less $3.1B cash. Reverse DCF (10% rate, 3% terminal): owner FCF of ~$2.0B (adj net income + after-tax interest - capex) must grow ~6% a year for 10 years; equity-only version (~$1.65B) needs ~5.5%. Revenue grew 13.6% a year 2020-2025 but FCF was flat (2020 $1.39B to 2025 $1.30B). About 16.2x 2026 adj EPS guide ($28). Own 5-year multiple range and peer multiples not computed.

status_reason: Quality is B and growth is strong, but the stock is up ~62% from its low to near the 52-week high, no clear misread is left, and the FTC consent order and BILL deal are still open.

feedback.fact: Corpay guides to $4.90/gal US fuel for the rest of 2026 and flat fuel spreads; Brent fell about 18% in a month, a headwind to the Vehicle segment (42% of revenue) if pump prices follow.
feedback.direction: contradicts overheat fuel tailwind if oil keeps falling

feedback.fact: Corporate Payments organic revenue +18% and 11% organic overall in Q3, with no sign of a spending slowdown in B2B payments volume yet.
